description: The protected-zone check on the Bash and PowerShell tools classified only the operand a verb WRITES, so a delete of a protected file or a move of it out of the zone was never examined: ``rm tools/cc/hooks/write_guard.py``, ``mv .claude/settings.json /tmp/x``, ``Remove-Item .espalier/integrity.json`` and ``Move-Item <hook> x`` all ALLOWED while a write to each path DENIED (walk 3, leg 4-C; driven at HEAD 2026-09-14 on the rehearsal's fixture: 40 of 47 Bash and 34 of 38 PowerShell class spellings allowed, identically on every protected kind and every root shape, and every alias, quoting and indirection spelling of the remove verb allowed while the write leg descended the same indirections). The secret-path check had the same shape one leg over: ``mv .env x``, ``tar -cf out.tar .env`` and ``Move-Item .env x`` allowed while ``cp .env x`` denied, and a top-level ``sh -c '<viewer> .env'`` allowed while the piped and interpreter forms denied. Fix (Section C52, DEF-795 + DEF-796): a tagged remove/relocate reader beside the write extractor on each shell (``iter_removed_or_relocated_operands``, ``iter_ps_removed_or_relocated_operands``, matched on the masked scan and read from the raw text) -- the remove verbs, ``git rm``, a ``find`` with a delete action, the source of ``mv`` (every source under ``-t DIR``), ``git mv`` and ``rename``, the ``Remove-Item`` family, ``Move-Item``'s and ``Rename-Item``'s source, a pipeline into a remove verb, ``[IO.File]::Move``'s source, and the interpreter delete and rename literals -- consumed by the renamed zone checks (``check_bash_for_protected_mutations``, ``check_powershell_for_protected_mutations``) with a new ``_encloses_protected`` predicate so a directory that encloses a protected path counts, and by the secret check for the move, archive, alias and interpreter-read effects plus the stream editors and the POSIX ``-c`` word. ``Clear-Content`` joined the PowerShell write verbs the same day (a truncation allowed beside a denied ``Set-Content``). The attempts below vary along VERB POSITION and INDIRECTION -- a wrapper, a quoted verb, a nested shell, an interpreter one-liner, a pipeline, an enclosing directory -- not only verb x zone, because a corpus flat along that axis reported an unchanged score while a first-draft anchor moved ninety verdicts (the axis-blind-gate lesson of 2026-08-03).
